prose: Rest of World reports that AI data centres are absorbing memory chips and pushing up smartphone costs, so the cheapest phones are disappearing. Existing models cost about 15% more this year and new launches about 25% more. Rises are steepest in India (21%), Asia-Pacific (19%) and the Middle East and Africa (18%), against 5% in the US. Chinese makers, about 60% of global shipments, have cut entry-level projects to chase margins. Counterpoint says phones that cost under $150 may now cost $250 to $300, and GSMA warns this could widen the digital divide for first-time users.
highlights: Memory shortage from AI data centres lifts phone costs.
Existing models up about 15%, new ones about 25%.
Chinese makers cut sub-$150 products for premium ones.
GSMA fears a wider digital divide.
Basis: most of the article was read.
